title: Geometric stalk calculation for a square of square-zero closed immersions
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $(f,f\prime):(X\hookrightarrow X\prime)\to(Y\hookrightarrow Y\prime)$ be a commutative square of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Both immersions are representable closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion], with square-zero ideal sheaves $\mathcal J$ on $X\prime$ and $\mathcal I$ on $Y\prime$. Identify the small etale sites across these thickenings, and regard $\mathcal I$ and $\mathcal J$, which are killed by their own ideals, as modules over $\mathcal O_Y$ and $\mathcal O_X$. Put $f^*\mathcal I=\mathcal O_X\otimes_{f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y}f^{-1}\mathcal I$; the canonical ideal map $f^*\mathcal I\to\mathcal J$ sends $a\otimes j$ to $\widetilde a\,f\prime{}^\sharp(j)$ for any local lift $\widetilde a$ of $a$ to $\mathcal O_{X\prime}$, independent of the lift because $\mathcal J^2=0$. Modules are [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and tensor is [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. A geometric point is a map from the spectrum of an algebraically closed field; its stalk is the colimit over pointed etale scheme neighbourhoods. Geometric stalk functors on any of these sites are exact and jointly detect isomorphisms of module sheaves. For each geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$, put $\bar y=f\bar x$, $A\prime=\mathcal O_{Y\prime,\bar y}$, $B\prime=\mathcal O_{X\prime,\bar x}$, $A=\mathcal O_{Y,\bar y}$, $B=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$, $I=\mathcal I_{\bar y}$, and $J=\mathcal J_{\bar x}$. The stalk maps form a commutative square of rings with surjections $A\prime\twoheadrightarrow A$, $B\prime\twoheadrightarrow B$ whose kernels are $I,J$; in particular $A=A\prime/I$, $B=B\prime/J$, and $I^2=J^2=0$. There is a canonical identification $(f^*\mathcal I)_{\bar x}\cong I\otimes_A B$. Under it, the canonical ideal map has stalk $q:I\otimes_A B\to J$, $i\otimes b\mapsto f\prime{}^\sharp(i)\widetilde b$, where $\widetilde b\in B\prime$ is any lift. The ideal of $Y\times_{Y\prime}X\prime$ in $X\prime$ has stalk $IB\prime$ at $\bar x$. Consequently the given square is cartesian, i.e. the canonical morphism $X\to Y\times_{Y\prime}X\prime$ is an isomorphism, if and only if $J=IB\prime$ at every such geometric point. Fibre products mean the sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. This statement imposes no flatness assumption.

The extended-ideal description is the quotient-ring calculation after an etale scheme base change.

proof.text: For either immersion write $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$. On affine etale scheme charts it is $\operatorname{Spec}(R/K)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $K^2=0$ by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Every prime contains $K$, so it is a thickening. By [lem-sfb-space-thickening-base-change], every scheme test of $i$ is a surjective closed immersion; [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-closed-immersion-universal-homeomorphism] makes it integral and universally injective. Thus [lem-sfb-space-integral-radicial-etale-invariance] gives an equivalence of the categories of chartwise etale algebraic-space objects. It preserves and reflects coverings: each base-change projection along $i$ is a homeomorphism by the thickening base-change theorem, so joint surjectivity is equivalent before and after base change. This is an equivalence of the enlarged etale sites. Apply [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]: restriction to scheme objects identifies their sheaf topoi with the small etale topoi, and the morphism for $i$ is induced by this very base-change functor. Consequently inverse image and direct image for $i$ are inverse equivalences on underlying sheaves. This supplies the common site interpretation for both thickenings; the structure ring sheaves themselves are related by their quotient map, computed next.

source.place: Tags 05ZH (theorem-topological-invariance) and 09ZX (lemma-base-change-thickening); spaces-properties.tex Tags 03G0, 03G1, 03G2 for enlarged/small etale site comparison and functoriality.

proof.text: Continue with $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$. For an affine etale chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to T$, put $V=Z\times_T U=\operatorname{Spec}(R/K)$ by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The section formula of [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction], applied to $\mathcal O_Z$, identifies $(i_*\mathcal O_Z)(U)$ with $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)=R/K$. The structure map on this chart is $R\twoheadrightarrow R/K$. Every etale scheme object is covered by affine open objects, so the structure-sheaf map is locally surjective, hence surjective as a sheaf map. Its kernel is the defining ideal $\mathcal L$. The site equivalence of Step 1 identifies $i_*\mathcal O_Z$ with $\mathcal O_Z$ on the common site: on each scheme test $U$ and its base change $V$, both are evaluated as $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$, compatibly with restriction. We obtain $0\to\mathcal I\to\mathcal O_{Y\prime}\to\mathcal O_Y\to0$ and $0\to\mathcal J\to\mathcal O_{X\prime}\to\mathcal O_X\to0$. Their ideal actions factor through the quotient ring sheaves, since a difference of two local lifts lies in the ideal and its product with that ideal is zero.

source.place: Tag 03MB (lemma-closed-immersion-ideals), first proof paragraph; spaces-properties.tex, lemma-pushforward-etale-base-change-modules; affine quotient description from Tag 01QO.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-space-geometric-points-conservative], the specified neighbourhood colimits are points of each etale topos and jointly detect isomorphisms of sheaves of sets. By [lem-sfb-ringed-site-point-exact], applied to the normalized ringed-site presentations at these points, module stalks are exact. An inverse of a bijective module map on underlying sheaves respects scalar multiplication, so the same stalk family detects module isomorphisms. Apply exact stalks to the two sequences of Step 2. This gives the surjections $A\prime\twoheadrightarrow A$, $B\prime\twoheadrightarrow B$ with kernels $I,J$. The sheaf square commutes, hence so does the stalk square; thus the upper ring map takes $I$ into $J$. Every pair of ideal germs has representatives on a common neighbourhood, where their product is zero, so $I^2=J^2=0$. The quotient identifications $A\cong A\prime/I$ and $B\cong B\prime/J$ are the explicit maps $[a\prime]\mapsto a\prime\bmod I$ and $[b\prime]\mapsto b\prime\bmod J$, bijective by the kernel and surjectivity assertions.

Apply [lem-sfb-space-geometric-points-conservative] to $f$ to identify the composite point with $\bar y$. The pullback-stalk formula of [lem-sfb-ringed-topos-pullback-stalk] then gives $(f^*\mathcal I)_{\bar x}\cong I\otimes_A B$, with its canonical pure-tensor normalization. For local sections $a$ and $i$, take a lift $\widetilde a$ along the locally surjective structure-sheaf quotient of Step 2 and set $a\otimes i\mapsto\widetilde a f\prime{}^\sharp(i)$. Two lifts differ by a section of $\mathcal J$, whose product with $f\prime{}^\sharp(i)\in\mathcal J$ is zero. This proves independence and gluing. Addition, scalar multiplication and the balancing relation hold after choosing lifts, because $f\prime{}^\sharp$ is a ring map and the square commutes. It therefore defines the asserted sheaf map. At the stalk every $b\in B$ lifts to $\widetilde b\in B\prime$ by Step 3. The pure-tensor normalization sends the stalk of this map to $q(i\otimes b)=f\prime{}^\sharp(i)\widetilde b$. Its independence from $\widetilde b$ is again $J^2=0$.

source.place: Tag 05V5 (lemma-pullback-stalk); spaces-properties.tex Tag 04K2(4); square-zero multiplication on the common sites.

proof.text: Put $P_0=Y\times_{Y\prime}X\prime$. By [lem-sfb-space-ideal-closed-subspace-correspondence], its closed-subspace ideal in $X\prime$ is $\mathcal K=\operatorname{im}((f\prime)^*\mathcal I\to\mathcal O_{X\prime})$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-geometric-points-conservative] and [lem-sfb-ringed-topos-pullback-stalk] to $f\prime$: the source stalk is $I\otimes_{A\prime}B\prime$, and multiplication sends $i\otimes b\prime$ to $f\prime{}^\sharp(i)b\prime$. Exactness of module stalks [lem-sfb-ringed-site-point-exact] identifies $\mathcal K_{\bar x}$ with the image of this map. Its elements are precisely finite sums of these products, which is the extended ideal $IB\prime$. No tensor-injectivity assertion is used.

source.place: Tag 03MB (lemma-closed-immersion-ideals) and paragraph after definition-inverse-image-closed-subspace; sites-modules.tex Tags 04EQ and 05V5.

proof.text: The commuting square makes $X$ a subspace of $P_0$ over $X\prime$, and $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal J$: pulled-back sections of $\mathcal I$ vanish after reduction to $X$. Every geometric point of $X\prime$ factors uniquely through $X$, since on the closed-immersion scheme base change its map to a field kills the square-zero ideal. Thus [lem-sfb-space-geometric-points-conservative] detects whether $\mathcal K\hookrightarrow\mathcal J$ is an isomorphism using exactly the points in the statement. By Step 5 this is equivalent to $IB\prime=J$ at every $\bar x$. By the bijection of [lem-sfb-space-ideal-closed-subspace-correspondence], equality $\mathcal K=\mathcal J$ is equivalent to equality of the two closed subspaces $P_0$ and $X$ of $X\prime$. In that case the canonical map $X\to P_0$ is the resulting isomorphism: a map over $X\prime$ into a closed subspace is unique, since its scheme base changes are closed embeddings, hence monomorphisms. Conversely, a canonical isomorphism identifies their kernel ideals and hence gives the same equality. This proves the cartesian criterion without a flatness hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 03MB, inclusion-reversing bijection; spaces-properties.tex Tag 04K5. Quotient-ring argument for the square in Tag 06BH.
